title: Three-Seventeen at the Blue Hour
theme: Reconciliation begins not with a grand apology, but with showing up before the morning ends.
story: At 3:17 a.m., the narrator receives a voicemail from their estranged father asking them to meet at the twenty-four-hour diner where he works. They bike through rain, replaying the message and remembering every unanswered call. The father admits he has no speech prepared, only coffee and a desire to see his child before sunrise. They do not solve the past, but share breakfast beneath the blue diner sign and leave with a real plan to meet again.
setting: A rain-slick city between 3:17 a.m. and dawn, moving from a dark apartment and empty bike lanes to a fluorescent roadside diner smelling of coffee, wet pavement, and toasted bread.
perspective: First person, an adult child narrating in the present while briefly flashing back to years of missed calls.
style_prompt: Indie pop / alt-R&B, 104 BPM; tender, restless, hopeful; intimate conversational lead vocal with a bruised upper register; rubbery synth bass, clean electric guitar, Rhodes piano, crisp drum kit, muted trumpet. Build toward a wide communal final chorus with a brief half-time bridge; glossy nocturnal production with rain-slick shimmer.
